# d-CCSSBU Methodology

## Common Steps for d-CCSSBU Chart Construction Algorithms {#sec-common-steps}

Let $D=\{e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_x\}$ denote the chronological sequence of cleaning events, where $e_t$ denotes the event observed at event-time index $t$. The following algorithm establishes the common framework for d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S chart construction for a fixed ordered-cluster parameter $d$. Selection of the optimal process-specific value of $d$ is addressed separately in the performance-optimization procedure.

**Step 1. Replace non-detects.** If any ND observations are present, replace them with the corresponding LOD or, when unavailable, the LOQ. (This conservative, worst-case replacement is commonly used in practice and is consistent with the general regulatory principle of applying scientifically justified, conservative treatment when exact quantitative information is unavailable. However, this step does not depend on this particular substitution; other scientifically justified approaches for handling ND observations can also be used.)

**Step 2. Conduct USL normalization.** Normalize each residue observation using $Z_{ti}=100X_{ti}/\mathrm{USL}_{ti}$. The resulting values are expressed as percentages of the applicable USL.

**Step 3. Calculate event-level location and scale statistics.** For the USL-normalized observations $R_t=\{Z_{t1},Z_{t2},\ldots,Z_{tp}\}$ associated with event $e_t$, calculate the location statistic of $e_t$ as $L_t=\mathrm{median}(R_t)$ and the scale statistic of $e_t$ as $S_t=\mathrm{MAD}(R_t)=\mathrm{median}\{|Z_{ti}-\mathrm{median}(R_t)|:i=1,\ldots,p\}$.

**Step 4. Create nominal Stage 3A and Stage 3B datasets.** Let $n_{3A}$ denote the target number of Stage 3A calibration events. If $x=n_{3A}$, define $D_{\mathrm{3A}}=\{e_1,\ldots,e_x\}$ and $D_{\mathrm{3B}}=\emptyset$. If $x>n_{3A}$, define $D_{\mathrm{3A}}=\{e_1,\ldots,e_{n_{3A}}\}$ and $D_{\mathrm{3B}}=\{e_{n_{3A}+1},\ldots,e_x\}$. The boundary between $D_{\mathrm{3A}}$ and $D_{\mathrm{3B}}$ is chronological; however, completion of the nominal Stage 3A period does not necessarily imply completion of calibration for every selected DAR cluster.

**Step 5. Create DAR clusters.** Retain a cleaning event for calibration if $\max_{i=1,\ldots,p}Z_{ti}\le100$, where 100 corresponds to 100\% of the applicable USL. Thus, all observations within the applicable specification remain eligible for calibration consideration, whereas an event containing an OOS observation is excluded from baseline calibration. For residue type DAR$_j$, create the DAR cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}=\{e_t:e_t\in D,\ \max_{i=1,\ldots,p}Z_{ti}\le100,\ \text{and is associated with DAR}_j\}$. Let $q$ denote the total number of DAR clusters represented in the calibration-eligible dataset. The DAR clusters form a partition of the calibration-eligible events, such that each calibration-eligible event belongs to exactly one DAR cluster. The parameter $d$, where $1\le d\le q$, denotes the number of ordered DAR clusters incorporated into chart calibration.

## d-CCSSBU-L Chart Construction Algorithm {#sec-dccssbu-l-algorithm}

The d-CCSSBU-L chart is constructed through above Steps 1--5 and Steps 6--15 below.

**Step 6. Order DAR clusters by location.** \textcolor{blue}{For each DAR cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}$, define its nominal Stage 3A component as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}\cap D_{\mathrm{3A}}$. If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}\neq\emptyset$, compute the cluster-level location statistic using its nominal Stage 3A events as $L_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}=\mathrm{median}\{L_t:e_t\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}\}$. If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}=\emptyset$, indicating that the DAR/API cluster is not represented during the nominal Stage 3A period, compute $L_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}=\mathrm{median}\{L_t:e_t\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}\}$ using its currently available calibration-eligible events. Order the DAR clusters such that $L_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(1)}}\ge L_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(2)}}\ge\cdots\ge L_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(q)}}$, where $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(1)}},\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(2)}},\ldots,\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(q)}}$ denote the resulting ordered DAR clusters.}

**Step 7. Identify Stage 3A events within ordered DAR clusters.** For each ordered cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, identify its nominal Stage 3A component as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},3A}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}\cap D_{\mathrm{3A}}$. Cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ may contain fewer than $n_{3A}$ nominal Stage 3A events and may have an empty Stage 3A component if the corresponding DAR/API is not represented during the nominal Stage 3A period.

**Step 8. Build the d-CCSSBU-L calibration dataset.**  
\textcolor{blue}{For a selected value $d\in\{1,2,\ldots,q\}$, construct the calibration dataset as
$D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)=\bigcup_{j=1}^{d}D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$.
For $j=1,\ldots,d$, repeat Steps 8.1--8.5 to determine the calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ for the selected ordered DAR cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$.}

**8.1.** \textcolor{blue}{ Set $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)=\varnothing$.}

**8.2.** \textcolor{blue}{ From $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, sequentially select, in chronological order, up to $n_{3A}$ events having distinct $L_t$ values within the current selection cycle. If fewer than $n_{3A}$ distinct $L_t$ values are represented in $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, exhaust the events with distinct $L_t$ values available in the current cycle. Add the selected events to $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$.}

**8.3.** \textcolor{blue}{ If $|D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)|=n_{3A}$, retain $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ as the calibration dataset for $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ and terminate Steps 8.1--8.5 for cluster $\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}$. Otherwise, proceed to Step 8.4.}


**8.4.** \textcolor{blue}{ Define the updated set of events as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}} =\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}\setminus D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$. From $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}$, sequentially select, in chronological order, up to $n_{3A}-|D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)|$ events having distinct $L_t$ values within the current selection cycle. If fewer than
$n_{3A}-|D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)|$ distinct $L_t$ values are represented in $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}$, exhaust the events with distinct $L_t$ values available in the current cycle. Append the newly selected events to $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ to update the calibration dataset.}

**8.5.** \textcolor{blue}{ If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}\setminus D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)\neq\varnothing$, return to Step 8.3. Otherwise, retain the currently available $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ as the calibration dataset for $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ and terminate Steps 8.1--8.5 for cluster $\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}$.}


**Step 9. Classify calibration status.** \textcolor{blue}{Let $n_{\mathrm{L},j}=\left|\{L_t:e_t\in D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)\}\right|$ denote the number of distinct $L_t$ values represented in the cluster-specific calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ for selected ordered DAR cluster $j$, and let $D_{\mathrm{Aug,L}}(d)=D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)\setminus D_{\mathrm{3A}}$ be the augmentation set. A selected ordered DAR cluster is classified as calibration-complete if $n_{\mathrm{L},j}=n_{3A}$ and calibration-limited if $n_{\mathrm{L},j}<n_{3A}$.}

A calibration-complete cluster retains its completed $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ unchanged at all subsequent analyses within the current calibration cycle. A calibration-limited cluster remains open to subsequently available calibration-eligible observations from the same cluster. At each subsequent analysis within the current calibration cycle, its provisional $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ is reconstructed from all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster, processed chronologically according to the selection procedure in Step 8. This process continues until the reconstructed $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ contains $n_{3A}$ events representing $n_{3A}$ distinct $L_t$ values. Once the cluster becomes calibration-complete, its $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ is frozen and is not subsequently reconstructed. The overall calibration status is classified into one of the following five cases.

**Case 1: Initial Stage 3A complete.** If $x=n_{3A}$ and every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, then the calibration dataset is finalized using the available events.

**Case 2: Initial Stage 3A calibration limited.** If $x=n_{3A}$ and at least one selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-limited, then the calibration dataset remains provisional because no post-Stage 3A events are available.

**Case 3: Stage 3B available and finalized without supplementation.** If $x>n_{3A}$, every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, and $D_{\mathrm{Aug,L}}(d)=\emptyset$, then the calibration dataset is finalized without using post-Stage 3A events.

**Case 4: Stage 3B available and finalized with supplementation.** If $x>n_{3A}$, every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, and $D_{\mathrm{Aug,L}}(d)\neq\emptyset$, then the calibration dataset is finalized after incorporating the chronologically selected post-Stage 3A events contained in $D_{\mathrm{Aug,L}}(d)$.

**Case 5: Stage 3B available and calibration still provisional.** If $x>n_{3A}$ and at least one selected ordered DAR cluster remains calibration-limited after all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster have been exhausted, then the calibration dataset remains provisional. When additional calibration-eligible observations from a calibration-limited cluster become available, its provisional $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ is reconstructed from all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster according to the chronological selection procedure in Step 8. This process continues until $n_{\mathrm{L},j}=n_{3A}$.


Under Cases 1, 3, and 4, once $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)$ is finalized, the selected cluster-specific calibration datasets $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L},j}(d)$ and the combined calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)$ are frozen for the current calibration cycle. Subsequently available routine Stage 3B observations cannot enter the finalized calibration dataset or replace previously selected calibration events. Under Cases 2 and 5, only calibration-limited clusters remain open to chronological supplementation.


**Step 10. Create sampling-location calibration strata.** Let $n_{\mathrm{Cal}}=|D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)|$ denote the size of the calibration dataset. For sampling location $r_s=1,\ldots,p$, create the calibration stratum $G_{r_s}=\{Z_{ir_s}:e_i\in D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)\}$. The calibration dataset is therefore partitioned into sampling-location strata $G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_p$.

**Step 11. Generate CCSSB bootstrap events.** For bootstrap replicate $b=1,\ldots,B$, sample one observation with replacement from each calibration stratum $G_{r_s}$ to obtain $X_{br_s}\in G_{r_s}$ for $r_s=1,\ldots,p$. Form the bootstrap event $e_b=\{X_{b1},X_{b2},\ldots,X_{bp}\}$ and smooth each sampled observation using $X_{br_s}^{*}=\max\{0,X_{br_s}+\varepsilon_{br_s}\}$, where $\varepsilon_{br_s}\sim N(0,h_{r_s}^{2})$ and $h_{r_s}=\max\{c_{\mathrm{smooth}}\times\mathrm{MAD}(G_{r_s}),h_{\min}\}$. In this study, $c_{\mathrm{smooth}}=0.5$, $h_{\min}=0.05$, and $B=20{,}000$. The resulting smoothed bootstrap event is $e_b^{*}=\{X_{b1}^{*},X_{b2}^{*},\ldots,X_{bp}^{*}\}$. The smoothing constant $c_{\mathrm{smooth}}=0.5$ and minimum bandwidth $h_{\min}=0.05$ were selected from a grid of candidate values based on the stability of bootstrap control-limit estimates and the consistency of charting conclusions across the study datasets. The bootstrap size $B=20{,}000$ was chosen to provide stable estimation of the upper-tail quantiles required for control-limit calibration. These quantities are implementation parameters rather than fixed methodological constants, and users may specify alternative values in the software implementation.

**Step 12. Calculate bootstrap location statistics.** For each bootstrap replicate $b=1,\ldots,B$, calculate the bootstrap event-level location statistic as $L_b^{*}=\mathrm{median}(X_{b1}^{*},X_{b2}^{*},\ldots,X_{bp}^{*})$. The collection $\{L_1^{*},L_2^{*},\ldots,L_B^{*}\}$ represents the CCSSB-calibrated location distribution associated with $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)$.

**Step 13. Estimate d-CCSSBU-L chart parameters.** Using the bootstrap location statistics, estimate the center line as $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}=\mathrm{median}(L_1^{*},L_2^{*},\ldots,L_B^{*})$ and estimate the upper control limit as $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}=\hat q_{1-\alpha}(L_1^{*},L_2^{*},\ldots,L_B^{*})$, where $\alpha=1/\mathrm{ARL}_0$ and $\hat q_{1-\alpha}$ denotes the empirical $(1-\alpha)$ quantile. In this study, $\mathrm{ARL}_0=740$ and therefore $\alpha=1/740$.

**Step 14. Construct the d-CCSSBU-L chart.** Calculate the event-level location statistic $L_t$ for each cleaning event and plot the chronological sequence $\{L_1,L_2,\ldots,L_x\}$ together with $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}$ and $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}$. Classify event $e_t$ as potentially out-of-control whenever $L_t>UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}$.

**Step 15. Perform Stage 3B monitoring.** Under Case 3 or Case 4, finalize the calibration dataset and chart parameters and apply them unchanged throughout routine Stage 3B monitoring. Under Case 3, all events in $D_{\mathrm{3B}}$ are monitored. Under Case 4, events contained in $D_{\mathrm{Aug,L}}(d)$ are used only for calibration and are excluded from routine monitoring. Under Case 2 or Case 5, maintain provisional calibration status until sufficient eligible events become available to finalize the chart.

## d-CCSSBU-S Chart Construction Algorithm {#sec-dccssbu-s-algorithm}

The d-CCSSBU-S chart is constructed through the above Steps 1--5 and Steps 6--15 below.

**Step 6. Order DAR clusters by scale.** \textcolor{blue}{For each DAR cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}$, define its nominal Stage 3A component as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}\cap D_{\mathrm{3A}}$. If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}\neq\emptyset$, compute the cluster-level scale statistic using its nominal Stage 3A events as $S_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}=\mathrm{median}\{S_t:e_t\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}\}$. If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j,3A}=\emptyset$, indicating that the DAR/API cluster is not represented during the nominal Stage 3A period, compute $S_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}=\mathrm{median}\{S_t:e_t\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_j}\}$ using its currently available calibration-eligible events. Order the DAR clusters such that $S_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(1)}}\ge S_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(2)}}\ge\cdots\ge S_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(q)}}$, where $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(1)}},\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(2)}},\ldots,\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(q)}}$ denote the resulting ordered DAR clusters.}

**Step 7. Identify Stage 3A events within ordered DAR clusters.** For each ordered cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, identify its nominal Stage 3A component as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},3A}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}\cap D_{\mathrm{3A}}$. Cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ may contain fewer than $n_{3A}$ nominal Stage 3A events and may have an empty Stage 3A component if the corresponding DAR/API is not represented during the nominal Stage 3A period.

**Step 8. Build the d-CCSSBU-S calibration dataset.**  \textcolor{blue}{For a selected value $d\in\{1,2,\ldots,q\}$, construct the calibration dataset as $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)=\bigcup_{j=1}^{d}D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$. For $j=1,\ldots,d$, repeat Steps 8.1--8.5 to determine the calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ for the selected ordered DAR cluster $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$.}

**8.1.** \textcolor{blue}{ Set $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)=\varnothing$.}

**8.2.** \textcolor{blue}{ From $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, sequentially select, in chronological order, up to $n_{3A}$ events having distinct $S_t$ values within the current selection cycle. If fewer than $n_{3A}$ distinct $S_t$ values are represented in $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$, exhaust the events with distinct $S_t$ values available in the current cycle. Add the selected events to $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$.}

**8.3.** \textcolor{blue}{ If $|D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)|=n_{3A}$, retain $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ as the calibration dataset for $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ and terminate Steps 8.1--8.5 for cluster $\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}$. Otherwise, proceed to Step 8.4.}

**8.4.** \textcolor{blue}{ Define the updated set of events as $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}=\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}\setminus D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$. From $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}$, sequentially select, in chronological order, up to $n_{3A}-|D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)|$ events having distinct $S_t$ values within the current selection cycle. If fewer than $n_{3A}-|D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)|$ distinct $S_t$ values are represented in $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}$, exhaust the events with distinct $S_t$ values available in the current cycle. Append the newly selected events to $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ to update the calibration dataset.}

**8.5.** \textcolor{blue}{ If $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)},\mathrm{update}}\setminus D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)\neq\varnothing$, return to Step 8.3. Otherwise, retain the currently available $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ as the calibration dataset for $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}}$ and terminate Steps 8.1--8.5 for cluster $\mathrm{DAR}_{(j)}$.}

**Step 9. Classify calibration status.** \textcolor{blue}{Let $n_{\mathrm{S},j}=\left|\{S_t:e_t\in D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)\}\right|$ denote the number of distinct $S_t$ values represented in the cluster-specific calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ for selected ordered DAR cluster $j$, and let $D_{\mathrm{Aug,S}}(d)=D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)\setminus D_{\mathrm{3A}}$ be the augmentation set. A selected ordered DAR cluster is classified as calibration-complete if $n_{\mathrm{S},j}=n_{3A}$ and calibration-limited if $n_{\mathrm{S},j}<n_{3A}$.}

The construction in Step 8 may produce three forms of a cluster-specific calibration dataset. First, $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ may contain $n_{3A}$ events representing $n_{3A}$ distinct $S_t$ values; this dataset is classified as calibration-complete. Second, it may contain $n_{3A}$ events but fewer than $n_{3A}$ distinct $S_t$ values because one or more $S_t$ values recur across different selection cycles; this dataset is classified as calibration-limited. Third, it may contain fewer than $n_{3A}$ events after all currently available calibration-eligible events in the cluster have been exhausted; this dataset is also classified as calibration-limited.

A calibration-complete cluster retains its completed $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ unchanged at all subsequent analyses within the current calibration cycle. A calibration-limited cluster remains open to subsequently available calibration-eligible observations from the same cluster. At each subsequent analysis within the current calibration cycle, its provisional $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ is reconstructed from all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster, processed chronologically according to the selection procedure in Step 8. This process continues until the reconstructed $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ contains $n_{3A}$ events representing $n_{3A}$ distinct $S_t$ values. Once the cluster becomes calibration-complete, its $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ is frozen and is not subsequently reconstructed. The overall calibration status is classified into one of the following five cases.

**Case 1: Initial Stage 3A complete.** If $x=n_{3A}$ and every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, then the calibration dataset is finalized using the available events.

**Case 2: Initial Stage 3A calibration limited.** If $x=n_{3A}$ and at least one selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-limited, then the calibration dataset remains provisional because no post-Stage 3A events are available.

**Case 3: Stage 3B available and finalized without supplementation.** If $x>n_{3A}$, every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, and $D_{\mathrm{Aug,S}}(d)=\emptyset$, then the calibration dataset is finalized without using post-Stage 3A events.

**Case 4: Stage 3B available and finalized with supplementation.** If $x>n_{3A}$, every selected ordered DAR cluster is calibration-complete, and $D_{\mathrm{Aug,S}}(d)\neq\emptyset$, then the calibration dataset is finalized after incorporating the chronologically selected post-Stage 3A events contained in $D_{\mathrm{Aug,S}}(d)$.

**Case 5: Stage 3B available and calibration still provisional.** If $x>n_{3A}$ and at least one selected ordered DAR cluster remains calibration-limited after Step 8 has processed all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster, then the calibration dataset remains provisional. When additional calibration-eligible observations from a calibration-limited cluster become available, its provisional $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ is reconstructed from all currently available calibration-eligible events from that cluster according to the chronological selection procedure in Step 8. This process continues until $n_{\mathrm{S},j}=n_{3A}$.

Under Cases 1, 3, and 4, once $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)$ is finalized, the selected cluster-specific calibration datasets $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S},j}(d)$ and the combined calibration dataset $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)$ are frozen for the current calibration cycle. Subsequently available routine Stage 3B observations cannot enter the finalized calibration dataset or replace previously selected calibration events. Under Cases 2 and 5, only calibration-limited clusters remain open. Their provisional cluster-specific calibration datasets are reconstructed when additional calibration-eligible observations become available, whereas calibration-complete clusters remain frozen.

**Step 10. Create sampling-location calibration strata.** Let $n_{\mathrm{Cal}}=|D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)|$ denote the size of the calibration dataset. For sampling location $r_s=1,\ldots,p$, create the calibration stratum $G_{r_s}=\{Z_{ir_s}:e_i\in D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)\}$. The calibration dataset is therefore partitioned into sampling-location strata $G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_p$.

**Step 11. Generate CCSSB bootstrap events.** For bootstrap replicate $b=1,\ldots,B$, sample one observation with replacement from each calibration stratum $G_{r_s}$ to obtain $X_{br_s}\in G_{r_s}$ for $r_s=1,\ldots,p$. Form the bootstrap event $e_b=\{X_{b1},X_{b2},\ldots,X_{bp}\}$ and smooth each sampled observation using $X_{br_s}^{*}=\max\{0,X_{br_s}+\varepsilon_{br_s}\}$, where $\varepsilon_{br_s}\sim N(0,h_{r_s}^{2})$ and $h_{r_s}=\max\{c_{\mathrm{smooth}}\times\mathrm{MAD}(G_{r_s}),h_{\min}\}$. In this study, $c_{\mathrm{smooth}}=0.5$, $h_{\min}=0.05$, and $B=20{,}000$. The resulting smoothed bootstrap event is $e_b^{*}=\{X_{b1}^{*},X_{b2}^{*},\ldots,X_{bp}^{*}\}$. The smoothing constant $c_{\mathrm{smooth}}=0.5$ and minimum bandwidth $h_{\min}=0.05$ were selected from a grid of candidate values based on the stability of bootstrap control-limit estimates and the consistency of charting conclusions across the study datasets. The bootstrap size $B=20{,}000$ was chosen to provide stable estimation of the upper-tail quantiles required for control-limit calibration. These quantities are implementation parameters rather than fixed methodological constants, and users may specify alternative values in the software implementation.

**Step 12. Calculate bootstrap scale statistics.** For each bootstrap replicate $b=1,\ldots,B$, calculate the bootstrap event-level scale statistic as $S_b^{*}=\mathrm{MAD}(X_{b1}^{*},X_{b2}^{*},\ldots,X_{bp}^{*})=\mathrm{median}\{|X_{br_s}^{*}-\mathrm{median}(X_{b1}^{*},X_{b2}^{*},\ldots,X_{bp}^{*})|:r_s=1,\ldots,p\}$. The collection $\{S_1^{*},S_2^{*},\ldots,S_B^{*}\}$ represents the CCSSB-calibrated scale distribution associated with $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)$.

**Step 13. Estimate d-CCSSBU-S chart parameters.** Using the bootstrap scale statistics, estimate the center line as $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}=\mathrm{median}(S_1^{*},S_2^{*},\ldots,S_B^{*})$ and estimate the upper control limit as $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}=\hat q_{1-\alpha}(S_1^{*},S_2^{*},\ldots,S_B^{*})$, where $\alpha=1/\mathrm{ARL}_0$ and $\hat q_{1-\alpha}$ denotes the empirical $(1-\alpha)$ quantile. In this study, $\mathrm{ARL}_0=740$ and therefore $\alpha=1/740$.

**Step 14. Construct the d-CCSSBU-S chart.** Calculate the event-level scale statistic $S_t$ for each cleaning event and plot the chronological sequence $\{S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_x\}$ together with $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}$ and $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}$. Classify event $e_t$ as potentially out-of-control whenever $S_t>UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}$.

**Step 15. Perform Stage 3B monitoring.** Under Case 3 or Case 4, finalize the calibration dataset and chart parameters and apply them unchanged throughout routine Stage 3B monitoring. Under Case 3, all events in $D_{\mathrm{3B}}$ are monitored. Under Case 4, events contained in $D_{\mathrm{Aug,S}}(d)$ are used only for calibration and are excluded from routine monitoring. Under Case 2 or Case 5, maintain provisional calibration status until sufficient eligible events become available to finalize the chart.

**Remark on d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts.** The proposed framework is presented using DAR data but may also be applied to CAR or Mic data when scientifically meaningful cluster heterogeneity exists. When the monitored population contains only one natural cluster such that $q=1$ and therefore $d=1$, the proposed methodology reduces to the corresponding one-cluster bootstrap location and scale charts.


## Selection of $d$ for the d-CCSSBU-L Chart {#sec-d-select-l}

For a given residue type, such as DAR, the following procedure evaluates candidate values of $d$ under additive location shifts and recommends a preferred value of $d$.

**Step 1. Construct d-CCSSBU-L charts for specific $d$.** Apply the d-CCSSBU-L chart construction algorithm in @sec-dccssbu-l-algorithm for each candidate value $d\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$. For each candidate $d$, obtain $D_{\mathrm{Cal,L}}(d)$, calibration status, calibration case, calibration size $n_{\mathrm{Cal}}$, bootstrap location sample $\{L_1^*(d),\ldots,L_B^*(d)\}$, chart parameters $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}(d)$ and $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}(d)$, and OOC counts $OOC_{ND}(d)$, $OOC_{3A}(d)$, and $OOC_{3B}(d)$.

**Step 2. Define the location-shift grid and benchmark model.** Calculate the mean and empirical standard deviation of the Stage 3A USL-normalized observations as $\mu_0=\operatorname{mean}\left(\{Z_{ti}:e_t\in D_{3A}\}\right)$ and $s_Z=sd\left(\{Z_{ti}:e_t\in D_{3A}\}\right)$, respectively. To maintain a nondegenerate benchmark distribution and shift scale when the USL-normalized observations exhibit little or no variability, define $\sigma_Z=\max(s_Z,h_{\min})$, where $h_{\min}=0.05$ is the minimum smoothing bandwidth used in the d-CCSSBU chart construction algorithm. The resulting in-control benchmark model is $Z\sim N(\mu_0,\sigma_Z^2)$. Let $\rho$ denote a location-shift magnitude expressed in units of $\sigma_Z$ and define the out-of-control (OC) shift grid as $\Omega_\rho=\{0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0\}$. The corresponding additive shift on the USL-normalized residue scale is $\rho\sigma_Z$.

**Step 3. Estimate candidate-specific ARL$_1$ curves.** For each candidate value $d$ and shift value $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, define $L_b^{*,\rho}(d)=L_b^*(d)+\rho\sigma_Z$ and estimate the OC signal probability as $p_1(d,\rho)=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B}I\{L_b^*(d)+\rho\sigma_Z>UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-L-boot}}(d)\}$. Estimate the corresponding average run length as $ARL_1(d,\rho)=1/p_1(d,\rho)$.

**Step 4. Evaluate benchmark ARL$_1$ performance.** For each shift value $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, evaluate the conventional $\bar X$ chart benchmark under the same additive shift $\rho\sigma_Z$ on the USL-normalized residue scale. Define the OC process mean as $\mu_1(\rho)=\mu_0+\rho\sigma_Z$. For subgroup size $n$, the OC subgroup mean follows $\bar Z_t\sim N\left(\mu_1(\rho),\sigma_Z^2/n\right)$. Calibrate the one-sided UCL as $UCL_{\bar X}=\mu_0+\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)\sigma_Z/\sqrt{n}$, where $\alpha=1/ARL_0$. Calculate the OC signal probability as $p_{1,\bar X}(\rho,n)=P\left(\bar Z_t>UCL_{\bar X}\mid\mu_1(\rho)\right)$ and the benchmark average run length as $ARL_{1,\bar X}(\rho,n)=1/p_{1,\bar X}(\rho,n)$.

**Step 5. Apply Rule 1 (ND-event protection).** Define $\mathcal D_1=\{d:OOC_{ND}(d)=0\}$.

**Step 6. Apply Rule 2 (Stage 3A protection).** Define $\mathcal D_2=\{d:OOC_{3A}(d)=0\}$. Construct the operationally admissible set $\mathcal A$ hierarchically as $\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ when nonempty; otherwise $\mathcal D_1$ when nonempty; otherwise $\mathcal D_2$ when nonempty; otherwise $\{1,\ldots,q\}$.

**Step 7. Apply Rule 3 (ARL$_1$ comparison).** For each candidate $d\in\mathcal A$ and shift value $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, compute the relative ARL ratio $R(d,\rho)=ARL_1(d,\rho)/ARL_{1,\bar X}(\rho,n)$. Define the worst-case relative ARL ratio as $W(d)=\max_{\rho\in\Omega_\rho}R(d,\rho)$ and the geometric mean relative ARL ratio as $G(d)=\exp\{|\Omega_\rho|^{-1}\sum_{\rho\in\Omega_\rho}\log R(d,\rho)\}$. Define the benchmark-superior set as $\mathcal U=\{d\in\mathcal A:W(d)\le1\}$.

**Step 8. Recommend value of $d$.** Two ARL$_1$ comparison cases are considered.

**U Case:** $\mathcal U\neq\varnothing$. At least one operationally admissible candidate remains benchmark-superior throughout the complete shift grid. Select $d_{\mathrm{rec}}=\max\mathcal U$ according to Rule 3.

**XO Case:** $\mathcal U=\varnothing$. No operationally admissible candidate remains benchmark-superior throughout the complete shift grid. Select the preliminary recommendation as $d_{\mathrm{rec}}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{d\in\mathcal A}W(d)$. If multiple candidates attain the same minimum value of $W(d)$, select the candidate with the smallest value of $G(d)$. If a tie still remains, select the largest value of $d$ according to Rule 3.

The decision path is classified into one of the following eight cases.

**Case 1:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ and U Case.

**Case 2:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ and XO Case.

**Case 3:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1$ and U Case.

**Case 4:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1$ and XO Case.

**Case 5:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_2$ and U Case.

**Case 6:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_2$ and XO Case.

**Case 7:** $\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$ and U Case.

**Case 8:** $\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$ and XO Case.

Apply Steps 1--8 separately to DAR, CAR, and Mic. Report the corresponding values of $s_Z$ and $\sigma_Z$ together with the resulting recommendations as $d_{\mathrm{DAR}}$, $d_{\mathrm{CAR}}$, and $d_{\mathrm{Mic}}$.


## Selection of $d$ for the d-CCSSBU-S Chart {#sec-d-select-s}

For a given residue type, such as DAR, the following procedure evaluates candidate values of $d$ under multiplicative increases in process variability and recommends a preferred value of $d$.

**Step 1. Construct d-specific d-CCSSBU-S charts.** Apply the d-CCSSBU-S chart construction algorithm in @sec-dccssbu-s-algorithm for each candidate value $d\in\{1,\ldots,q\}$. For each candidate $d$, obtain $D_{\mathrm{Cal,S}}(d)$, calibration status, calibration case, calibration size $n_{\mathrm{Cal}}$, bootstrap scale sample $\{S_1^*(d),\ldots,S_B^*(d)\}$, chart parameters $CL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}(d)$ and $UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}(d)$, and OOC counts $OOC_{ND}(d)$, $OOC_{3A}(d)$, and $OOC_{3B}(d)$.

**Step 2. Define the variability-ratio grid and benchmark model.** Calculate the mean and empirical standard deviation of the Stage 3A USL-normalized observations as $\mu_0=\operatorname{mean}\left(\{Z_{ti}:e_t\in D_{3A}\}\right)$ and $s_Z=sd\left(\{Z_{ti}:e_t\in D_{3A}\}\right)$, respectively. To maintain a nondegenerate benchmark distribution when the USL-normalized observations exhibit little or no variability, define $\sigma_Z=\max(s_Z,h_{\min})$, where $h_{\min}=0.05$ is the minimum smoothing bandwidth used in the d-CCSSBU chart construction algorithm. The resulting in-control benchmark model is $Z\sim N(\mu_0,\sigma_Z^2)$. Let $\rho$ denote the multiplicative variability ratio and define the OC variability-ratio grid as $\Omega_\rho=\{1.05,1.10,1.20,1.50,2.00,2.25\}$.

**Step 3. Estimate candidate-specific ARL$_1$ curves.** For each candidate value $d$ and variability ratio $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, define the shifted bootstrap scale statistic as $S_b^{*,\rho}(d)=\rho S_b^*(d)$. Estimate the OC signal probability as $p_1(d,\rho)=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B}I\{\rho S_b^*(d)>UCL_{\mathrm{CCSSBU-S-boot}}(d)\}$ and estimate the corresponding average run length as $ARL_1(d,\rho)=1/p_1(d,\rho)$.

**Step 4. Evaluate benchmark ARL$_1$ performance.** For each variability ratio $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, evaluate the conventional $S$ chart benchmark under the same multiplicative increase in process variability. Define the OC process standard deviation as $\sigma_1(\rho)=\rho\sigma_Z$. Assuming normality and subgroup size $n$, the subgroup standard deviation satisfies $(n-1)S_t^2/\sigma_1^2(\rho)\sim\chi^2_{n-1}$. Calibrate the IC one-sided upper control limit as $UCL_S=\sigma_Z\sqrt{\chi^2_{1-\alpha,n-1}/(n-1)}$, where $\alpha=1/ARL_0$ and $\chi^2_{1-\alpha,n-1}$ denotes the $(1-\alpha)$ quantile of the chi-squared distribution with $n-1$ degrees of freedom. Calculate the OC signal probability as $p_{1,S}(\rho,n)=P\left(S_t>UCL_S\mid\sigma_1(\rho)\right)$ and the benchmark average run length as $ARL_{1,S}(\rho,n)=1/p_{1,S}(\rho,n)$.

**Step 5. Apply Rule 1 (ND-event protection).** Define $\mathcal D_1=\{d:OOC_{ND}(d)=0\}$.

**Step 6. Apply Rule 2 (Stage 3A protection).** Define $\mathcal D_2=\{d:OOC_{3A}(d)=0\}$. Construct the operationally admissible set $\mathcal A$ hierarchically as $\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ when nonempty; otherwise $\mathcal D_1$ when nonempty; otherwise $\mathcal D_2$ when nonempty; otherwise $\{1,\ldots,q\}$.

**Step 7. Apply Rule 3 (ARL$_1$ comparison).** For each candidate $d\in\mathcal A$ and variability ratio $\rho\in\Omega_\rho$, compute the relative ARL ratio $R(d,\rho)=ARL_1(d,\rho)/ARL_{1,S}(\rho,n)$. Define the worst-case relative ARL ratio as $W(d)=\max_{\rho\in\Omega_\rho}R(d,\rho)$ and the geometric mean relative ARL ratio as $G(d)=\exp\{|\Omega_\rho|^{-1}\sum_{\rho\in\Omega_\rho}\log R(d,\rho)\}$. Define the benchmark-superior set as $\mathcal U=\{d\in\mathcal A:W(d)\le1\}$.

**Step 8. Recommend a value of $d$.** Two ARL$_1$ comparison cases are considered.

**U Case:** $\mathcal U\neq\varnothing$. At least one operationally admissible candidate remains benchmark-superior throughout the complete variability-ratio grid. Select $d_{\mathrm{rec}}=\max\mathcal U$ according to Rule 3.

**XO Case:** $\mathcal U=\varnothing$. No operationally admissible candidate remains benchmark-superior throughout the complete variability-ratio grid. Select $d_{\mathrm{rec}}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{d\in\mathcal A}W(d)$. If multiple candidates attain the same minimum value of $W(d)$, select the candidate with the smallest value of $G(d)$. If a tie still remains, select the largest value of $d$ according to Rule 3.

The decision path is classified into one of the following eight cases.

**Case 1:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ and U Case.

**Case 2:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1\cap\mathcal D_2$ and XO Case.

**Case 3:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1$ and U Case.

**Case 4:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_1$ and XO Case.

**Case 5:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_2$ and U Case.

**Case 6:** $\mathcal A=\mathcal D_2$ and XO Case.

**Case 7:** $\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$ and U Case.

**Case 8:** $\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$ and XO Case.

Apply Steps 1--8 separately to DAR, CAR, and Mic. Report the resulting recommendations as $d_{\mathrm{DAR}}$, $d_{\mathrm{CAR}}$, and $d_{\mathrm{Mic}}$. 

# Chart-Selection Algorithm for Mic Data: Poisson $u$ Chart or d-CCSSBU Charts {#sec-poisson}

Unlike DAR and CAR measurements, Mic observations are nonnegative count data and share a common microbial USL. When microbial results are reported below a microbial detection limit (e.g., <1 CFU/swab), they are converted to count values according to the site's microbiological reporting convention before analysis. Count data are often appropriately modeled by the Poisson distribution, and extensive literature exists on the statistical analysis and capability assessment of Poisson processes [@Poisson2016; @Discrete2023; @Anscombe1948; @Freeman1950]. Therefore, a Poisson $u$ chart is preferred when the Mic process is compatible with the Poisson distribution. When the Poisson assumption is not supported by the data, d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts are applied instead.

For cleaning event $e_t$, let $X_{ti}$ denote the microbial count at sampling location $i$ and let $p_t$ denote the number of observed sampling locations. Missing observations are excluded, and each observed sampling location is treated as one comparable exposure unit because all results use the same CFU/swab basis.

**Step 1. Calculate event-level microbial statistics.** For event $e_t$, calculate the total microbial count as $Y_t=\sum_{i=1}^{p_t}X_{ti}$ and the microbial density as $u_t=Y_t/p_t$. For display on the common percentage-of-USL scale, calculate $u_t^*=100u_t/\mathrm{USL}$. Conduct all Poisson-model assessments using the original integer counts $X_{ti}$ rather than the normalized values.

**Step 2. Create nominal Stage 3A and Stage 3B datasets.** If $x= n_{3A}$, define $D_{\mathrm{3A}}=\{e_1,\ldots,e_x\}$ and $D_{\mathrm{3B}}=\emptyset$. If $x>n_{3A}$, define $D_{\mathrm{3A}}=\{e_1,\ldots,e_{n_{3A}}\}$ and $D_{\mathrm{3B}}=\{e_{n_{3A}+1},\ldots,e_x\}$.

**Step 3. Select the Poisson-assessment dataset.** Apply one of the following data-availability cases.

**Case 1: All available counts are zero.** If all available Mic counts are zeros, do not construct a Poisson $u$ chart because $\hat\lambda=0$ produces a degenerate center line and upper control limits. Apply the d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts. Unlike the Poisson $u$ chart, the CCSSB calibration procedure incorporates smoothing with a positive minimum bandwidth and therefore remains applicable even when all observed counts are identical.

**Case 2: Stage 3A counts are zero and Stage 3B contains a positive count.** If all Stage 3A counts are zero but at least one Stage 3B count is positive, use all available Mic observations as the Poisson-assessment dataset. The resulting chart parameters are estimated from all currently available observations and retained for monitoring of future events.

**Case 3: Stage 3A contains a positive count.** If Stage 3A contains at least one positive Mic count, use the Stage 3A observations as the Poisson-assessment and calibration dataset. Reserve Stage 3B events for monitoring when the Poisson $u$ chart is selected.

**Step 4. Estimate the Poisson rate.** Using the dataset selected in Step 3, estimate the microbial rate per sampled location as $\hat\lambda=\sum_tY_t/\sum_tp_t$. Under the Poisson model, each individual count satisfies $X_{ti}\sim\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$, with $E(X_{ti})=\mathrm{Var}(X_{ti})=\lambda$.

**Step 5. Assess Poisson goodness of fit.** Calculate a Pearson-type goodness-of-fit statistic from the individual microbial counts. Generate parametric bootstrap datasets from $\mathrm{Poisson}(\hat\lambda)$ using the same number of observations as the assessment dataset, recalculate the statistic for each bootstrap dataset, and estimate the goodness-of-fit p-value as the proportion of bootstrap statistics at least as large as the observed statistic. Classify the Poisson goodness-of-fit condition as satisfied when the bootstrap p-value exceeds the prespecified significance level $\alpha_{\mathrm{GOF}}$.

**Step 6. Assess overdispersion.** Calculate the dispersion ratio as $\phi=s_X^2/\bar X$, where $\bar X$ and $s_X^2$ are the sample mean and sample variance of the individual counts in the Poisson-assessment dataset. Evaluate overdispersion using the prespecified bootstrap or analytical criterion implemented in the analysis. Classify the no- stepsubstantial-overdispersion condition as satisfied when the observed dispersion is not significantly greater than that expected under $\mathrm{Poisson}(\hat\lambda)$.

**Step 7. Select the Mic charting method.** Select the Poisson $u$ chart when the assessment dataset contains at least one positive count, the Poisson goodness-of-fit condition is satisfied, and no substantial overdispersion is detected. Otherwise, select the d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts.

Under an accepted Poisson model, a separate scale chart is unnecessary because the mean and variance are both governed by $\lambda$. When the Poisson model is unsupported, the d-CCSSBU charts monitor location and scale separately without requiring a count-distribution assumption.

**Step 8. Construct the Poisson $u$ chart when selected.** Use the Poisson calibration dataset selected in Step 3 to estimate the center line as $\bar u=\sum_tY_t/\sum_tp_t$. Express the center line on the normalized scale as $CL_u^*=100\bar u/\mathrm{USL}$.

For event $e_t$, calculate the exact one-sided Poisson upper control limit for the total count as $UCL_{Y,t}=q_{1-\alpha}\{\mathrm{Poisson}(p_t\bar u)\}$, where $\alpha=1/\mathrm{ARL}_0$ and $q_{1-\alpha}$ denotes the corresponding Poisson quantile. Calculate the event-specific density limit as $UCL_{u,t}=UCL_{Y,t}/p_t$ and its normalized value as $UCL_{u,t}^*=100UCL_{u,t}/\mathrm{USL}$. In this study, $\mathrm{ARL}_0=740$ and therefore $\alpha=1/740$.

Plot $\{u_1^*,u_2^*,\ldots,u_x^*\}$ against cleaning-event order together with $CL_u^*$ and the event-specific limits $\{UCL_{u,1}^*,UCL_{u,2}^*,\ldots,UCL_{u,x}^*\}$. Classify event $e_t$ as potentially out-of-control when $u_t^*>UCL_{u,t}^*$. A lower control limit is not used because decreases in microbial counts represent improved rather than adverse cleaning performance.

Under Case 3, retain the Stage 3A rate estimate and control limits for Stage 3B monitoring. Under Case 2, estimate the chart parameters using all currently available observations and retain the resulting parameters for monitoring of future events.


**Step 9. Construct d-CCSSBU charts when selected.** The d-CCSSBU-L chart monitors the event-level median of the normalized Mic observations, whereas the d-CCSSBU-S chart monitors their event-level MAD. Apply these charts to all-zero datasets, datasets that do not support the Poisson model, or datasets exhibiting substantial overdispersion.

**Comments.** The algorithm used the exact Poisson $u$ chart, which has a discrete upper control limit derived from the exact Poisson distribution. A conventional $3\sigma$ Poisson $u$ chart uses the same monitoring statistic but approximates the upper control limit by $UCL_t=\bar u_t+3\sqrt{\frac{\bar u_t}{n_t}},$ where $\bar u_t$ is the estimated average nonconformity rate (and equals $\bar \mu_t^*$  in Step 8) and $n_t$ is the inspection opportunity associated with the $t$th event. Because the exact Poisson $u$ chart accounts for the discrete Poisson distribution directly, differences between the exact and $3\sigma$ limits can occur, especially when $\bar u_t$ or $n_t$ is small as in CV data.



# Codes

Applications of the proposed algorithms and methodologies to the Equipment A and Equipment B case studies are presented in this section.

## Selection of $d$ for the d-CCSSBU-L Chart

```{r d-ccssbu-l-function}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
d_ccssbu_l <- function(file,
                       equipment_label="Equipment A",
                       residue_type="DAR",
                       sheet=residue_type,

                       # Design parameters
                       d=3,
                       n_stage3A_events=10,
                       target_ARL0=740,
                       B=20000,
                       c_smooth=0.5,
                       h_min=0.05,
                       seed=123,
                       location_distinct_digits=10,

                       # Calibration eligibility
                       location_eligibility_threshold=100,

                       # Cluster definition
                       cluster_col="USL",
                       cluster_group_cols=NULL,
                       cluster_round_digits=10,

                       # Input columns
                       event_col="Event",
                       location_col="Location",
                       result_col="Result",
                       lod_col="LOD",
                       loq_col="LOQ",
                       usl_col="USL",

                       # Output controls
                       plot_chart=TRUE,
                       save_outputs=TRUE,
                       output_dir=file.path(getwd(),"d_CCSSBU_L_Charts"),
                       return_bootstrap_matrix=FALSE,
                       keep_bootstrap_statistics=TRUE){

  required_pkgs <- c("readxl","dplyr","ggplot2","stringr","readr","matrixStats")
  
  missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[!(required_pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages()))]

  if (length(missing_pkgs)>0) {stop("Please install the following package(s): ",paste(missing_pkgs,collapse=", "))}

  if (target_ARL0<=1) stop("target_ARL0 must be greater than 1.")
  
  if (B<1 || B!=as.integer(B)) stop("B must be a positive integer.")
  
  if (d<1 || d!=as.integer(d)) stop("d must be a positive integer.")
  
  if (n_stage3A_events<1 || n_stage3A_events!=as.integer(n_stage3A_events)) {
    stop("n_stage3A_events must be a positive integer.")}
  
  if (c_smooth<0) stop("c_smooth must be nonnegative.")
  
  if (h_min<0) stop("h_min must be nonnegative.")

  if (location_distinct_digits<0 ||location_distinct_digits!=as.integer(location_distinct_digits)){
    stop("location_distinct_digits must be a nonnegative integer.")}

  if (location_eligibility_threshold<=0) {stop("location_eligibility_threshold must be positive.")}
  
  if (save_outputs && !dir.exists(output_dir)) {dir.create(output_dir,recursive=TRUE)}

  alpha <- 1/target_ARL0

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper functions
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {
    x <- x[!is.na(x) & is.finite(x)]
    if (length(x)==0) return(NA_real_)
    median(abs(x-median(x)),na.rm=TRUE)
  }

  is_nd_result <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(toupper(as.character(x)))
    x %in% c("ND","N.D.","N/D","NON-DETECT","NONDETECT","NON DETECT","NOT DETECT")}

  extract_event_number <- function(x) {
    x <- trimws(as.character(x))
    direct <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
    extracted <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(x,"\\d+$")))

    dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(direct) ~ direct,
      !is.na(extracted) ~ extracted,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_)
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x,probs) {
    x <- x[!is.na(x) & is.finite(x)]
    if (length(x)==0) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(stats::quantile(x,probs=probs,na.rm=TRUE,type=7,names=FALSE))
  }

  safe_name <- function(x) {gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+","_",as.character(x))}

  safe_plot_text <- function(x) {gsub("_","-",as.character(x))}

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Read and validate data
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  all_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(file)

  if (!(sheet %in% all_sheets)) {
    stop("Requested sheet was not found: ",sheet,
         ". Available sheets: ",paste(all_sheets,collapse=", "))
  }

  dat_raw <- readxl::read_excel(file,sheet=sheet) |>
    dplyr::rename_with(~stringr::str_trim(.x))

  result_col_actual <- result_col

  if (!(result_col_actual %in% names(dat_raw)) &&
      residue_type %in% names(dat_raw)) {
    result_col_actual <- residue_type
  }

  required_cols <- c(
    event_col,location_col,result_col_actual,lod_col,
    loq_col,usl_col,cluster_col,cluster_group_cols
  )

  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols,names(dat_raw))

  if (length(missing_cols)>0) {
    stop("Sheet ",sheet," is missing required columns: ",
         paste(missing_cols,collapse=", "))
  }

  message("d-CCSSBU-L equipment = ",equipment_label)
  message("Residue type = ",residue_type)
  message("Sheet used = ",sheet)
  message("Cluster column = ",cluster_col)
  message("d = ",d,
          "; n_stage3A_events = ",n_stage3A_events,
          "; target ARL0 = ",target_ARL0,
          "; alpha = ",signif(alpha,5),
          "; B = ",B,
          "; c_smooth = ",c_smooth,
          "; h_min = ",h_min,
          "; eligibility threshold = ",location_eligibility_threshold,
          "; seed = ",seed)

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1. Replace non-detects.
  # Step 2. Conduct USL normalization.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  normalized_data <- dat_raw |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Equipment=equipment_label,
      ResidueType=residue_type,
      Event=extract_event_number(.data[[event_col]]),
      Location=trimws(as.character(.data[[location_col]])),
      Result_chr=trimws(as.character(.data[[result_col_actual]])),
      ND_flag=is_nd_result(Result_chr),
      Result_raw=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Result_chr)),
      LOD=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[lod_col]])),
      LOQ=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[loq_col]])),
      USL=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[usl_col]])),
      Cluster_Value_Raw=.data[[cluster_col]],
      Cluster_Value_Numeric=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[cluster_col]])),
      
      Cluster_Value=dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(Cluster_Value_Numeric) ~ as.character(round(Cluster_Value_Numeric,cluster_round_digits)),
        TRUE ~ trimws(as.character(Cluster_Value_Raw))),
      
      Result_Replacement_Source=dplyr::case_when(
        ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~ "ND replaced by LOD",
        ND_flag & is.na(LOD) & !is.na(LOQ) ~ "ND replaced by LOQ",
        ND_flag & is.na(LOD) & is.na(LOQ) ~ "Removed: ND with missing LOD and LOQ",
        !ND_flag & !is.na(Result_raw) ~ "Observed Result",
        !ND_flag & is.na(Result_raw) ~"Removed: missing or nonnumeric Result",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      
      Result_ND_Replaced=dplyr::case_when(
        ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~ LOD,
        ND_flag & is.na(LOD) & !is.na(LOQ) ~ LOQ,
        !ND_flag & !is.na(Result_raw) ~ Result_raw,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_)
    )

  n_removed_nd <- sum(normalized_data$ND_flag &is.na(normalized_data$LOD) &is.na(normalized_data$LOQ),na.rm=TRUE)

  n_removed_result <- sum(!normalized_data$ND_flag & is.na(normalized_data$Result_raw),  na.rm=TRUE )

  if (n_removed_nd>0) {warning(n_removed_nd," ND row(s) removed because both LOD and LOQ were missing.")}

  if (n_removed_result>0) {warning(n_removed_result," non-ND row(s) removed because Result was missing or nonnumeric.")}

  normalized_data <- normalized_data |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !(ND_flag & is.na(LOD) & is.na(LOQ)),
      !(!ND_flag & is.na(Result_raw)),
      !is.na(Event),
      !is.na(Location),
      Location!="",
      !is.na(USL),
      USL>0,
      !is.na(Cluster_Value),
      Cluster_Value!="",
      !is.na(Result_ND_Replaced)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Normalized=100*Result_ND_Replaced/USL) |>
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(Normalized))

  if (nrow(normalized_data)==0) {stop("No usable observations remain after ND replacement and normalization.")}

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Construct DAR/API cluster key
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (is.null(cluster_group_cols)) {
    normalized_data <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::mutate(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key=paste(ResidueType,cluster_col,Cluster_Value,sep=" | "))
  } else {
    group_key_df <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cluster_group_cols)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(),~trimws(as.character(.x)))) |>
      as.data.frame()

    group_key <- do.call(paste,c(group_key_df,sep=" | "))

    normalized_data$d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key <- paste(
      normalized_data$ResidueType,
      group_key,
      cluster_col,
      normalized_data$Cluster_Value,sep=" | ")
  }

  normalized_data <- normalized_data |>
    dplyr::select(
      Equipment,ResidueType,Event,Location,Result_chr,Result_raw,
      LOD,LOQ,USL,Cluster_Value,d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key,ND_flag,
      Result_Replacement_Source,Result_ND_Replaced,Normalized,
      dplyr::everything()
    )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Chronological event sequence D={e1,...,ex}
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  event_levels <- normalized_data |>
    dplyr::distinct(Event) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Event) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Event_index=dplyr::row_number())

  normalized_data <- normalized_data |>
    dplyr::left_join(event_levels,by="Event") |>
    dplyr::arrange(Event_index,Location)

  event_cluster_check <- normalized_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Event,Event_index) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_clusters_in_event=dplyr::n_distinct(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key),
      cluster_keys=paste(unique(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key),collapse="; "), 
      .groups="drop") |>
    dplyr::filter(n_clusters_in_event>1)

  if (nrow(event_cluster_check)>0) {
    stop(
      "Some cleaning events belong to more than one DAR cluster. ",
      "This violates the algorithm's partition assumption. ",
      "Check whether cluster_col='",cluster_col,
      "' and cluster_group_cols are constant within each event. ",
      "Example event(s): ",
      paste(head(event_cluster_check$Event,10),collapse=", ")
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3. Calculate event-level L_t and S_t.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  event_statistics <- normalized_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(Event,Event_index) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Equipment=dplyr::first(Equipment),
    ResidueType=dplyr::first(ResidueType),
    d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key=dplyr::first(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key),
    Cluster_Value=dplyr::first(Cluster_Value),
    L_t=median(Normalized,na.rm=TRUE),
    S_t=mad_unscaled(Normalized),
    Max_Z_t=max(Normalized,na.rm=TRUE),
    Min_Z_t=min(Normalized,na.rm=TRUE),
    m_t=dplyr::n(),
    n_locations_observed=dplyr::n_distinct(Location),
    n_zero_values=sum(Normalized==0,na.rm=TRUE),
    n_positive_values=sum(Normalized>0,na.rm=TRUE),
    n_ND_values=sum(ND_flag,na.rm=TRUE),
    all_ND_event=all(ND_flag),
    n_distinct_normalized_values=dplyr::n_distinct(
      round(Normalized,location_distinct_digits),
      na.rm=TRUE
    ),
    .groups="drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    all_normalized_values_identical=n_distinct_normalized_values==1,
    L_t_distinct_key=round(L_t,location_distinct_digits),
    Location_Calibration_Eligible=Max_Z_t<=location_eligibility_threshold) |>dplyr::arrange(Event_index)
  

  x <- nrow(event_statistics)

  if (x<n_stage3A_events) {stop("At least ",n_stage3A_events," cleaning events are required. Current x = ",x,".")}

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 4. Create nominal Stage 3A and Stage 3B datasets.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  D_3A_event_index <- seq_len(n_stage3A_events)
  D_3A_event_ids <- event_statistics$Event[match(D_3A_event_index,event_statistics$Event_index)]

  if (x==n_stage3A_events) {
    D_3B_event_index <- integer(0)
    D_3B_event_ids <- event_statistics$Event[0]
    analysis_stage <- "Initial Stage 3A analysis"
  } else {
    D_3B_event_index <- seq.int(n_stage3A_events+1L,x)
    D_3B_event_ids <- event_statistics$Event[match(D_3B_event_index,event_statistics$Event_index)]
    analysis_stage <- "Stage 3B analysis with post-Stage 3A events available"
  }

  event_statistics <- event_statistics |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      In_D_3A=Event_index %in% D_3A_event_index,
      In_D_3B=Event_index %in% D_3B_event_index
    )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 5. Create calibration-eligible DAR clusters.
  # Eligibility is Max_Z_t <= 100, including equality.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  event_statistics_eligible <- event_statistics |>
    dplyr::filter(Location_Calibration_Eligible)

  if (nrow(event_statistics_eligible)==0) {
    stop(
      "No event is eligible for d-CCSSBU-L calibration. ",
      "All events have Max_Z_t > ",location_eligibility_threshold,"."
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 6. Order DAR clusters by location.
  #
  # Use eligible nominal Stage 3A events when available.
  # If the cluster is absent from nominal Stage 3A, use all
  # currently available calibration-eligible events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  cluster_summary <- event_statistics_eligible |>
    dplyr::group_by(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key,Cluster_Value) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_events_cluster=dplyr::n(),
      n_events_cluster_in_D_3A=sum(In_D_3A),
      n_events_cluster_in_D_3B=sum(In_D_3B),
      first_event_index_cluster=min(Event_index),
      max_L_t_cluster=max(L_t),
      min_L_t_cluster=min(L_t),
      n_all_ND_events_cluster=sum(all_ND_event),
      L_cluster=if (any(In_D_3A)) {median(L_t[In_D_3A],na.rm=TRUE)} else {median(L_t,na.rm=TRUE)},
      S_cluster_diagnostic=if (any(In_D_3A)) {median(S_t[In_D_3A],na.rm=TRUE)} else {median(S_t,na.rm=TRUE)},
      cluster_ordering_basis=if (any(In_D_3A)) {"Eligible nominal Stage 3A events"} else {
        paste0("All currently available eligible events; ","cluster absent from nominal Stage 3A")},
      .groups="drop") |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(L_cluster),first_event_index_cluster,d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key) |>
    dplyr::mutate(ordered_cluster_rank=dplyr::row_number())

  q <- nrow(cluster_summary)

  if (q==0) {stop("No eligible DAR clusters are available for calibration.")}
  
  if (d>q) {
    warning("Input d = ",d," is larger than q = ",q,". Setting d = q.")
    d <- q}

  selected_cluster_summary <- cluster_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(ordered_cluster_rank<=d) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ordered_cluster_rank)

  selected_cluster_keys <-selected_cluster_summary$d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key
  
cluster_ordering_lookup <- cluster_summary |>
  dplyr::select(
    d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key,
    L_cluster,
    S_cluster_diagnostic,
    cluster_ordering_basis,
    ordered_cluster_rank
  )

event_statistics <- event_statistics |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    cluster_ordering_lookup,
    by = "d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Event_index) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    In_first_d_ordered_clusters =
      d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key %in% selected_cluster_keys
  )

# Step 8 operates on calibration-eligible events, but those events
# must also retain the Step 6 cluster-ordering information.
event_statistics_eligible <- event_statistics |>
  dplyr::filter(Location_Calibration_Eligible) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Event_index)

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 7. Identify nominal Stage 3A events within clusters.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
stage3A_ordered_cluster_summary <- event_statistics_eligible |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    ordered_cluster_rank,
    d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key,
    Cluster_Value,
    L_cluster,
    cluster_ordering_basis
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_stage3A_component = sum(In_D_3A),
    stage3A_event_index = paste(
      Event_index[In_D_3A],
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    stage3A_event_ids = paste(
      Event[In_D_3A],
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(ordered_cluster_rank)

    
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 8. Build D_Cal,L(d).
  # For each selected ordered DAR cluster j = 1,...,d,
  # Steps 8.1-8.5 construct D_Cal,L,j(d).
  #
  # Step 8 constructs the calibration dataset only.
  # Calibration-complete and calibration-limited status are
  # classified afterward in Step 9.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  select_cluster_calibration_events <- function(cluster_key_j) {

    candidates <- event_statistics_eligible |>
      dplyr::filter(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key == cluster_key_j) |>
      dplyr::arrange(Event_index) |>
      dplyr::mutate(L_t_distinct_key = round(L_t,location_distinct_digits))

    if (nrow(candidates) == 0) {
      return(
        list(
          selected_index = integer(0),
          selected_ids = numeric(0),
          selection_detail = candidates,
          selection_cycle_summary = data.frame(),
          n_selected_events = 0L,
          n_distinct_L_t = 0L,
          n_selection_cycles = 0L,
          cluster_events_exhausted = TRUE
        )
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 8.1.
    #
    # Initialize the cluster-specific calibration dataset:
    #
    # D_Cal,L,j(d) = empty set.
    #
    # The first current selection set is the complete set of
    # currently available calibration-eligible events belonging
    # to the selected ordered DAR cluster.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    selected <- candidates[0, , drop = FALSE]
    remaining <- candidates
    cycle_detail_list <- list()
    selection_cycle <- 0L

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Steps 8.2-8.5.
    #
    # Continue until either:
    #
    # 1. D_Cal,L,j(d) contains n3A events; or
    # 2. all currently available calibration-eligible events
    #    in the selected cluster have been exhausted.
    #
    # Reaching n3A events terminates Step 8 construction, but
    # does not itself determine calibration status. Step 9
    # determines status from the number of distinct L_t values
    # represented in the constructed dataset.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    while (nrow(selected) < n_stage3A_events && nrow(remaining) > 0) {

      selection_cycle <- selection_cycle + 1L

      n_needed <- n_stage3A_events - nrow(selected)

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Step 8.2 when selection_cycle == 1.
      #
      # From the complete cluster, process events in
      # chronological order and retain the earliest event for
      # each distinct L_t value in the first selection cycle.
      #
      # Two outcomes are possible:
      #
      # 1. At least n3A distinct L_t values are available:
      #    select n3A events having distinct L_t values.
      #
      # 2. Fewer than n3A distinct L_t values are available:
      #    exhaust the distinct L_t values represented in the
      #    first cycle and add those events to D_Cal,L,j(d).
      #
      # Step 8.4 when selection_cycle > 1.
      #
      # From the updated event set, process events in
      # chronological order and select up to the remaining
      # required number of events having distinct L_t values
      # within the current cycle.
      #
      # An L_t value selected in an earlier cycle may appear
      # again in the current cycle through a different event.
      # Distinctness is required within the current cycle, not
      # across all cycles.
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      cycle_selected <- remaining |>
        dplyr::arrange(Event_index) |>
        dplyr::distinct(
          L_t_distinct_key,
          .keep_all = TRUE
        ) |>
        dplyr::slice_head(n = n_needed) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          Selection_Cycle = selection_cycle,
          Selection_Order_Within_Cycle =
            dplyr::row_number()
        )

      if (nrow(cycle_selected) == 0) {
        break
      }

      # Add or append the events selected in the current cycle
      # to D_Cal,L,j(d).
      selected <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        selected,
        cycle_selected
      )

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Step 8.3.
      #
      # This condition is checked immediately after the current
      # selection is added to D_Cal,L,j(d).
      #
      # In the first cycle, if n3A events were selected, they
      # necessarily represent n3A distinct L_t values because
      # Step 8.2 selected distinct L_t values. Step 8 therefore
      # terminates without applying Steps 8.4-8.5.
      #
      # In a later cycle, reaching n3A events also terminates
      # Step 8 construction. However, repeated L_t values may
      # exist across cycles, so Step 9 must subsequently classify
      # the constructed dataset.
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      if (nrow(selected) == n_stage3A_events) {

        cycle_detail_list[[selection_cycle]] <- data.frame(
          d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key = cluster_key_j,
          Selection_Cycle = selection_cycle,
          Step_8_Substep = if (
            selection_cycle == 1L
          ) {
            "Step 8.2 followed by Step 8.3"
          } else {
            "Step 8.4 followed by Step 8.3"
          },
          n_requested_at_start = n_needed,
          n_selected_in_cycle = nrow(cycle_selected),
          selected_event_index = paste(
            cycle_selected$Event_index,
            collapse = ", "
          ),
          selected_event_ids = paste(
            cycle_selected$Event,
            collapse = ", "
          ),
          selected_L_t_keys = paste(
            cycle_selected$L_t_distinct_key,
            collapse = ", "
          ),
          n_selected_total_after_cycle = nrow(selected),
          n_remaining_after_cycle =
            nrow(remaining) - nrow(cycle_selected),
          Step_8_3_target_reached = TRUE,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Step 8.3 termination.
        break
      }

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Step 8.4.
      #
      # Because fewer than n3A events have been selected, define
      # the updated event set by removing the selected events
      # from the cluster candidate set.
      #
      # Removal occurs at the event level. Other events having
      # an L_t value already selected in an earlier cycle remain
      # in the updated set and may be selected in a later cycle.
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      remaining <- remaining |>
        dplyr::filter(
          !(Event_index %in% cycle_selected$Event_index)
        ) |>
        dplyr::arrange(Event_index)

      cycle_detail_list[[selection_cycle]] <- data.frame(
        d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key = cluster_key_j,
        Selection_Cycle = selection_cycle,
        Step_8_Substep = if (
          selection_cycle == 1L
        ) {
          "Step 8.2 followed by Step 8.4"
        } else {
          "Step 8.4"
        },
        n_requested_at_start = n_needed,
        n_selected_in_cycle = nrow(cycle_selected),
        selected_event_index = paste(
          cycle_selected$Event_index,
          collapse = ", "
        ),
        selected_event_ids = paste(
          cycle_selected$Event,
          collapse = ", "
        ),
        selected_L_t_keys = paste(
          cycle_selected$L_t_distinct_key,
          collapse = ", "
        ),
        n_selected_total_after_cycle = nrow(selected),
        n_remaining_after_cycle = nrow(remaining),
        Step_8_3_target_reached = FALSE,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Step 8.5.
      #
      # If events remain in the updated event set, return to
      # Step 8.3 and continue to Step 8.4 for another selection
      # cycle.
      #
      # If no events remain, retain the currently available
      # D_Cal,L,j(d) and terminate Steps 8.1-8.5.
      #
      # The while-loop condition implements this decision:
      #
      # - nrow(remaining) > 0: another cycle is performed;
      # - nrow(remaining) == 0: construction terminates.
      # --------------------------------------------------------
    }

    # If Step 8.3 terminated immediately after reaching the
    # target, remove the events selected in the final cycle from
    # the remaining set for accurate exhaustion diagnostics.
    selected_event_index <- selected$Event_index

    remaining_after_construction <- candidates |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !(Event_index %in% selected_event_index)
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(Event_index)

    selected <- selected |>
      dplyr::arrange(
        Selection_Cycle,
        Selection_Order_Within_Cycle,
        Event_index
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Selection_Order = dplyr::row_number(),

        Selection_Round = paste0("Chronological distinct-L_t selection cycle ",Selection_Cycle),

        Calibration_Source = dplyr::if_else(In_D_3A,"D_3A","D_Aug,L(d)")
      )

    n_selected_events <- nrow(selected)

    n_distinct_L_t <- dplyr::n_distinct(selected$L_t_distinct_key,na.rm = TRUE)

    cluster_events_exhausted <-    nrow(remaining_after_construction) == 0

    selection_cycle_summary <- if (length(cycle_detail_list) > 0) {
      dplyr::bind_rows(cycle_detail_list)
    } else {data.frame()}

    # Step 8 returns the constructed calibration dataset and
    # construction diagnostics. It does not classify the cluster.
    list(
      selected_index = selected$Event_index,
      selected_ids = selected$Event,
      selection_detail = selected,
      selection_cycle_summary =
        selection_cycle_summary,
      n_selected_events = n_selected_events,
      n_distinct_L_t = n_distinct_L_t,
      n_selection_cycles = selection_cycle,
      cluster_events_exhausted =
        cluster_events_exhausted
    )
  } #select_cluster_calibration_events

  cluster_selection_list <- lapply(
    selected_cluster_keys,
    select_cluster_calibration_events
  )

  names(cluster_selection_list) <- selected_cluster_keys

  D_Cal_L_event_index_by_cluster <- lapply(
    cluster_selection_list,
    function(z) z$selected_index
  )

  D_Cal_L_event_ids_by_cluster <- lapply(
    cluster_selection_list,
    function(z) z$selected_ids
  )

  D_Cal_L_event_index <- sort(unique(unlist(
    D_Cal_L_event_index_by_cluster,
    use.names = FALSE
  )))

  if (length(D_Cal_L_event_index) == 0) {
    stop("D_Cal,L(d) is empty. Bootstrap limits cannot be estimated.")
  }

  D_Cal_L_event_ids <- event_statistics$Event[
    match(
      D_Cal_L_event_index,
      event_statistics$Event_index
    )
  ]

cluster_selection_detail <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(cluster_selection_list), function(j) {

    cluster_key_j <- names(cluster_selection_list)[[j]]
    detail_j <- cluster_selection_list[[j]]$selection_detail

    if (nrow(detail_j) == 0) {return(NULL)}

    cluster_rank_j <- selected_cluster_summary |>
      dplyr::filter(d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key == cluster_key_j) |>
      dplyr::pull(ordered_cluster_rank)

    if (length(cluster_rank_j) != 1) {stop("Could not identify exactly one ordered-cluster rank for ",cluster_key_j,".")}

    detail_j |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        selected_cluster_key = cluster_key_j,
        selected_cluster_rank = as.integer(cluster_rank_j)
      )
  })
)

if (is.null(cluster_selection_detail) ||nrow(cluster_selection_detail) == 0) {cluster_selection_detail <- tibble::tibble()}



 # if (is.null(cluster_selection_detail)) {cluster_selection_detail <- data.frame()}

cluster_selection_cycle_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(cluster_selection_list), function(j) {

    cluster_key_j <- names(cluster_selection_list)[[j]]
    cycle_j <- cluster_selection_list[[j]]$selection_cycle_summary

    if (nrow(cycle_j) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    cluster_rank_j <- selected_cluster_summary |>
      dplyr::filter(
        d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key == cluster_key_j
      ) |>
      dplyr::pull(ordered_cluster_rank)

    if (length(cluster_rank_j) != 1) {
      stop(
        "Could not identify exactly one ordered-cluster rank for ",
        cluster_key_j,
        "."
      )
    }

    cycle_j |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        selected_cluster_key = cluster_key_j,
        selected_cluster_rank = as.integer(cluster_rank_j)
      )
  })
)

if (is.null(cluster_selection_cycle_summary) ||
    nrow(cluster_selection_cycle_summary) == 0) {
  cluster_selection_cycle_summary <- tibble::tibble()
}


 # if (is.null(cluster_selection_cycle_summary)) {cluster_selection_cycle_summary <- data.frame()}

  D_Aug_L_event_index <- sort(setdiff(D_Cal_L_event_index,D_3A_event_index))

  D_Aug_L_event_ids <- event_statistics$Event[match(D_Aug_L_event_index,event_statistics$Event_index)]

  n_Cal <- length(D_Cal_L_event_index)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 9. Classify calibration status.
  #
  # Step 8 has already completed construction of each
  # D_Cal,L,j(d). Step 9 does not select, add, remove, or
  # replace calibration events. It only classifies the
  # constructed cluster-specific calibration datasets.
  #
  # The Step 8 construction can produce three dataset forms,
  # which Step 9 classifies into two calibration statuses:
  #
  # 1. n_Cal_j = n3A and n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j = n3A:
  #    Calibration complete.
  #
  # 2. n_Cal_j = n3A and n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j < n3A:
  #    Calibration limited. The dataset contains n3A events,
  #    but some L_t values recur across different selection
  #    cycles.
  #
  # 3. n_Cal_j < n3A and n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j < n3A:
  #    Calibration limited. All currently available eligible
  #    events in the cluster have been exhausted before n3A
  #    events can be obtained.
  #
  # Thus, the formal classification is:
  # - Calibration complete if n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j = n3A.
  # - Calibration limited if n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j < n3A.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  

  cluster_calibration_status <- selected_cluster_summary |>
    dplyr::rowwise() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      n_Cal_j = length(D_Cal_L_event_index_by_cluster[[d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key]]),

      n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j = dplyr::n_distinct(
        event_statistics$L_t_distinct_key[event_statistics$Event_index %in% D_Cal_L_event_index_by_cluster[[d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key]] ],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      n_repeated_L_t_events_j =  n_Cal_j - n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j,

      n_selection_cycles_j =cluster_selection_list[[d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key]]$n_selection_cycles,

      cluster_events_exhausted_j =cluster_selection_list[[d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key]]$cluster_events_exhausted,

      n_Aug_j = sum(D_Cal_L_event_index_by_cluster[[d_CCSSBU_L_cluster_key]] %in% D_Aug_L_event_index),

      calibration_complete_j =n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j == n_stage3A_events,

      calibration_limited_j = n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j < n_stage3A_events,

      calibration_status_j = dplyr::if_else(
        calibration_complete_j,
        "Calibration complete",
        "Calibration limited"
      ),

      calibration_status_reason_j = dplyr::case_when(

  calibration_complete_j ~ paste0(
    "The cluster-specific calibration dataset contains ",
    n_stage3A_events,
    " events representing ",
    n_stage3A_events,
    " distinct L_t values."
  ),

  n_Cal_j == n_stage3A_events &&
    n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j < n_stage3A_events ~ paste0(
      "The cluster-specific calibration dataset contains ",
      n_stage3A_events,
      " events but only ",
      n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j,
      " distinct L_t values because one or more L_t values ",
      "recur across different selection cycles."
    ),

  n_Cal_j < n_stage3A_events ~ paste0(
    "The cluster-specific calibration dataset contains only ",
    n_Cal_j,
    " events and ",
    n_distinct_L_t_Cal_j,
    " distinct L_t values after all currently available ",
    "eligible events were exhausted."
  ),

  TRUE ~
    "Calibration status could not be characterized."
  )
    ) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  all_selected_clusters_complete <- all(
    cluster_calibration_status$calibration_complete_j
  )

  any_selected_cluster_limited <- any(
    cluster_calibration_status$calibration_limited_j
  )
  
  case_label <- NA_character_
  case_name <- NA_character_
  case_definition <- NA_character_
  calibration_finalized <- FALSE

  if (x==n_stage3A_events && all_selected_clusters_complete) {
    case_label <- "Case 1"
    case_name <- "Initial Stage 3A complete"
    case_definition <- paste0(
      "x=n3A and every selected ordered DAR cluster is ",
      "calibration-complete. The calibration dataset is finalized ",
      "using the available events."
    )
    calibration_finalized <- TRUE
  } else if (x==n_stage3A_events &&
             any_selected_cluster_limited) {
    case_label <- "Case 2"
    case_name <- "Initial Stage 3A calibration limited"
    case_definition <- paste0(
      "x=n3A and at least one selected ordered DAR cluster is ",
      "calibration-limited. No post-Stage 3A events are available, ",
      "so the calibration dataset remains provisional."
    )
  } else if (x>n_stage3A_events &&
             all_selected_clusters_complete &&
             length(D_Aug_L_event_index)==0) {
    case_label <- "Case 3"
    case_name <- paste0(
      "Stage 3B available and finalized without supplementation"
    )
    case_definition <- paste0(
      "x>n3A, every selected ordered DAR cluster is ",
      "calibration-complete, and D_Aug,L(d) is empty. ",
      "The calibration dataset is finalized without supplementation."
    )
    calibration_finalized <- TRUE
  } else if (x>n_stage3A_events &&
             all_selected_clusters_complete &&
             length(D_Aug_L_event_index)>0) {
    case_label <- "Case 4"
    case_name <- paste0(
      "Stage 3B available and finalized with supplementation"
    )
    case_definition <- paste0(
      "x>n3A, every selected ordered DAR cluster is ",
      "calibration-complete, and D_Aug,L(d) is nonempty. ",
      "The calibration dataset is finalized after chronological ",
      "post-Stage 3A supplementation."
    )
    calibration_finalized <- TRUE
  } else if (x>n_stage3A_events &&
             any_selected_cluster_limited) {
```
